papers.title: Holistic Semiconductor Lithography for the Age of AI
authors_raw: Marco Pieters,Executive Vice President and Chief Technology Ofﬁcer
ASML, Veldhoven, The Netherlands
affils_raw: Artiﬁcial intelligence (AI) is generating strong demand for semiconductor chips,
especially at the leading edge. This dynamic is fueling innovation in the
semiconductor industry to continue with geometrical scaling, with the accompanying
beneﬁts of reduced power consumption and increased operating speed, and to speed
up the development of device and circuit stacking in the third dimension to further
increase density and improve connectivity. In this presentation, we will present
ASML’s holistic lithography technology roadmap designed to meet the needs of the
AI revolution. Our roadmap brings together EUV lithography (both 0.33 NA and high
NA), DUV lithography (including 193-nm immersion), computational lithography,
wafer inspection and metrology, and increasingly sophisticated control loops to
improve resolution, overlay accuracy (including post-bonding overlay), process
control, productivity, and to reduce the cost of technology. We will highlight the role
of high-NA EUV lithography in reducing process complexity and cost by eliminating
multi-patterning and, for logic integrated circuits, re-enabling 2D design and routing.
We will discuss ASML’s expanding role in advanced packaging and 3D integration to
enable further density increase and connectivity speedup. We will demonstrate that,
while AI drives demand for more powerful semiconductor chips, it is also part of
holistic semiconductor lithography, enhancing modelling, simulation, metrology, and
control loops to improve lithography performance and process control. Finally,
advancing technology in the AI era is a shared challenge of the entire semiconductor
ecosystem, requiring continued innovation and collaboration across research
partners, equipment, material, and EDA suppliers, and chipmakers.

papers.title: The Next Leap in Image Sensors: Pixels and Beyond in the AI Era
authors_raw: Yusuke Oike, CTO / Senior Vice President, R&D
Sony Semiconductor Solutions, Atsugi, Japan
affils_raw: Relentless advances in pixel technology have transformed image sensors, delivering
unprecedented imaging performance. Looking ahead, the next leap goes beyond
pixels to reshape camera systems in response to rapid AI advancement. This talk
highlights advances pushing pixel limits for faithful imaging, AI-leveraged imaging
that enriches the photographic experience, and reliable multimodal sensing that
provides low-latency observations physical AI needs to see and act in the real world.

papers.title: At the End of the Copper Tunnel, There Is Light
authors_raw: Matt Murphy, Chairman and Chief Executive Ofﬁcer,
Marvell, Santa Clara, CA
affils_raw: For over half a century, semiconductor progress was deﬁned by transistor density.
But with the dawn of AI, the bottleneck has shifted from how fast a chip can think to
how fast the collective can share its thoughts. Whether connecting chiplets inside a
package, AI servers within a rack, rows of servers across a datacenter, or bridging
remote datacenters into a single cluster — connectivity is the key to AI efﬁciency.
Copper interconnects are the backbone of computing today, and pushing their limits
of speed, reach, and power is an art that very few possess. But as AI pushes
boundaries, copper hits a wall. Behind that wall is the light of optical links that will
shape the AI datacenter. The move from copper to optics represents a structural
rearchitecting of AI infrastructure, and one of the most consequential opportunities
We’ll discuss what drives this shift, how different optical technologies serve each
layer of the AI datacenter, and what enables silicon photonics, optical DSPs, and
co-packaged optics to make this transition economically viable at volume — allowing
AI scale to continue and greater intelligence to be realized.

papers.title: From Silicon to Deployed Infrastructure: Redeﬁning the Semiconductor Design Challenge at Hyperscale
authors_raw: Rani Borkar, President, Azure Hardware Systems and Infrastructure
Microsoft, Redmond, WA
affils_raw: The demands of hyperscale AI infrastructure are redefining the semiconductor design
challenge, because the distance between great silicon and great deployed
infrastructure is wider and more consequential than ever. The optimization aperture
continues to expand, with networking and memory architecture playing an
increasingly first-order role in shaping design decisions across the stack, from die
and package through rack, cluster, datacenter, and even regional infrastructure. At
the same time, the center of gravity is shifting away from any single accelerator and
toward composing the right system from purpose-built CPUs, high-performance
storage, and heterogeneous, disaggregated AI accelerators. At production scale,
reliability, manageability, and the ability to rapidly bring new hardware generations
into production also become central to translating design advantage into deployed
value. This plenary explores how those demands are reshaping hardware tradeoffs
and linking silicon choices to the economics of delivering AI at global scale.
